title: Ephemeral Mirror Orchestration for Private/VPC Deployments (PRD)
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Problem: Customers running Private/VPC deployments require a robust, auditable mechanism to stage artifacts and operator changes into air-gapped environments with minimal egress while preserving fast rollback, integrity verification, and predictable upgrade windows. This PRD defines an "ephemeral mirror" orchestration pattern: a temporary, operator-controlled image/artifact mirror that can be created, validated, and torn down as part of an upgrade or bootstrap to minimize permanent external surfaces.
background: Existing private upgrades rely on long-lived mirrors or on-demand operator egress. Long-lived mirrors increase attack surface and operational burden; ad-hoc egress can violate customer compliance. We've received engineering and customer feedback requesting: (1) a short-lived mirror option synchronized under operator control, (2) integrity guarantees (checksums/signatures), and (3) deterministic rollback and verification steps for air-gapped clusters.
goals: 1) Define operator flows to create an ephemeral mirror for a scheduled upgrade/bootstrapping window. 2) Specify network constraints and minimal allowlists required. 3) Define integrity checks, KMS interactions, and acceptance criteria for a successful stage. 4) Ensure deterministic rollback and operator idempotency. 5) Provide observability hooks required by platform and customer SREs.
out_of_scope: Permanent mirror lifecycle management (long-term mirror health), physical-media/manual import procedures, and automated provisioning of customer-side bastions. This PRD focuses on operator-driven ephemeral mirrors and their orchestration protocol only.
requirements: 1) Mirror Lifecycle: operator can create an ephemeral mirror endpoint (HTTPS/OCI) in the customer's VPC or designated mirror subnet with a TTL and explicit deletion step. 2) Minimal Egress Policy: list of required egress destinations and ports (CIDR or FQDN) must be documented; operator uses short-lived credentials and a presigned upload channel when supported. 3) Integrity: every artifact and image must be checksum'd (SHA-256) and signed by Redwood's release signing key; operator must verify signatures against a key-resolver endpoint or provided public key. 4) Bandwidth & Throttling: mirror sync supports rate-limited transfers, resume support, and per-job bandwidth caps to respect customer network constraints. 5) Atomic Staging: staged content must expose a two-phase commit marker: STAGE_READY -> VERIFIED -> PROMOTE. If verification fails, the operator must auto-abort and optionally retry per policy. 6) Observability: progress, bytes transferred, verification results, and per-artifact status must be emitted to the private control plane (or retained locally for air-gapped installs) and mapped to console traces. 7) RBAC & Audit: operator actions create immutable audit events with identity, timestamp, and artifact hashes. 8) Offline Validation Mode: support a validation-only run that verifies local artifacts against provided manifests without performing promotion. 9) Rollback: defined rollback operation that reverses promotions and can restore previous operator images and configs. 10) Multi-site: support for staging mirrors in multi-site environments with cross-check reconciliation and conflict detection.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Create & Tear Down: Operator can create a mirror endpoint in a test VPC using only documented minimal allowlist rules; mirror endpoint is automatically deleted after TTL. 2) Egress Policy Validation: An audit run exists verifying that required egress destinations match the allowlist; if extra egress is required an explicit escalation flow is triggered. 3) Signature & Checksum Verification: For 100% of staged artifacts, operator verifies SHA-256 checksums and validates signatures successfully against the configured key; failures are recorded and cause stage abort. 4) Bandwidth Controls: In a constrained network test (simulated 10 Mbps), the operator completes a staged sync within an expected extended window and respects configured bandwidth caps without saturating the network. 5) Two-phase Promotion: Promotion only occurs after VERIFICATION passes for all artifacts; partial promotions are not allowed. 6) Rollback Simulation: A canary promotion can be rolled back by the operator within the defined rollback window and cluster state returns to pre-promotion state (configs and running operator image). 7) Observability: Traces and transfer metrics are available in the private control plane UI and match on-host logs for reconciled runs. 8) Audit Trail: All mirror lifecycle events (create, upload chunk, verify, promote, delete) are present in audit logs with artifact hashes and operator identity. 9) Security: KMS key rotation during a staged run does not lead to unsigned artifacts being promoted; rotation must either be transparent or cause stage abort with human intervention. 10) Docs & Runbook: Runbook validated with Solutions Engineering and customer pilot; at least two customer pilots completed with feedback incorporated.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal): implement operator prototype and run e2e tests against an internal air-gapped lab. Phase 2 (beta): invite 3 pilot customers from the enterprise funnel for 1:1 onboarding and runbook validation. Phase 3 (GA): rollout as an opt-in private-deploy feature; provide console controls for ephemeral mirror creation and TTL. Rollout includes migrations for customers using long-lived mirrors to the ephemeral pattern with a provided validation script.
monitoring_and_alerting: Emit metrics: mirror.create.count, mirror.delete.count, transfer.bytes, transfer.errors, verify.failures, promote.success, rollback.invoked. Alerts: verify.failures > 0 for >5 min, transfer.errors spike, mirror left beyond TTL. Provide SLOs for operator availability during mirror lifecycle (99.9% for control-plane actions).
rollback_criteria: 1) Verification failure on any artifact. 2) Missing KMS key or signature verification errors. 3) Sustained transfer failures > 3 attempts per artifact. 4) Operator health degraded (reconciliation loop failing or restarts > 5 in 10m). On rollback trigger, operator must mark the promotion aborted, revert any partial config changes, and if a rollback fails, create a high-severity incident with automated diagnostics bundle.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Customers misconfigure allowlists leading to failed upgrades. Mitigation: provide an allowlist validator tool and preflight check that simulates mirror creation. Risk: Malicious actor intercepts temporary mirror endpoints. Mitigation: short TTLs, mTLS between operator and mirror, signed manifests. Risk: KMS rotation causing promotion failures. Mitigation: require key-rotation-aware verification and explicit operator steps; add a pre-stage KMS compatibility check. Risk: Customer bandwidth saturation during sync. Mitigation: enforce conservative default bandwidth caps and provide explicit bandwidth override with customer consent.
